findings.title: Passage release can delete a replacement owner's claim
findings.problem: releasePassage reads the claim, checks its owner, then removes the path in a separate storage operation. A takeover can replace the claim between that check and the removal. The owner check therefore does not enforce the documented guarantee that release removes only the caller's own claim.
findings.failure_scenario: A synthesis fails without saving a record, and its release is delayed by storage latency. Release reads owner A near the lease boundary. After the lease expires, B takes over and uploads its claim. A's delayed remove then deletes B's claim. C can now create a fresh claim while B is synthesising, so B and C both pay to voice the same passage. The daily spending cap still holds, but one-synthesis-per-passage exclusion does not.
findings.fix: Make takeover and owner-checked release atomic, for example through a transactional database claim table/RPC with conditional update and delete operations. Add a concurrency test that pauses release after its owner read, completes a takeover, then resumes release and verifies that the replacement claim remains and a third caller stays busy. The existing sequential ownership test does not exercise this interleaving.

assessment: Request changes: passage-claim release can race with lease takeover and permit duplicate paid synthesis. Review was limited to the supplied changes; tests were not executed. The underlying narrate-lib.mjs normalization was not supplied, so its clinical-number equivalence rules could not be independently verified.
